text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Aerospatiale and Dassault Aviation now interested in joint bid for Thomson-CSF.
-- Suez sells last 49% of Banque Indosuez to Credit Agricole for 11.9 billion francs.
-- Employers federation and trade unions agree on higher unemployment benefits and lower contributions to Unedic unemployment fund.
-- October industrial output down 1.2 percent.
-- Elf Aquitaine and Gaz de France utilities supplier teaming up on North Sea gas projects.
-- Sanofi aims to become one of the world's top ten pharmaceutical groups.
-- Schneider to sell Spie Batignolles to employees and Amec for a billion francs.
-- Credit Immobilier de France confirms interest in Credit Foncier buyout.
-- Fidel Castro announces clinical trials of AIDS vaccine on 24 young scientists.
LA TRIBUNE
-- France's highest administrative court says Thomson privatisation requires specific decree.
-- Moulinex increases registered capital by 500 million francs.
-- Utilities group Electricite de France posts 3.7 billion year profit.
-- Tax officials search home of Cie Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier to track down several millions of francs in commissions.
-- In an interview, Renault chairman Louis Schweitzer expects price war on new cars to continue and warns against overvalued euro.
L'AGEFI
-- Carte Bleue and Visa sign accord to issue 10 million credit cards.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Paris wants to sell 300 Leclerc main battle tanks to Saudi Arabia.
-- European Commission says French tax breaks on investments in overseas territories are incompatible with free market competition and disqualifies tax deductions on ships over 100 tons.
-- U.S. pressure gets Brussels to allow imports of genetically-modified corn.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- French air force cancels training flights until new year because fuel budget has dried up.
LE PARISIEN
-- Cafe and restaurant sales of champagne by the glass have risen by 67 percent in the past five years.
